purpose: Reference for whoever generates SFT entries for the Among Us agent.
The base model has never played this game and does not know the terms,
the maps, the legality rules or the social language. Everything it needs
to avoid writing nonsense lives here.
Read this before generating. An entry that violates ROLES, VENT_NETWORKS,
or TASK_SEQUENCE is defective and validate.py will reject it.

what_the_game_is.shape: social deduction, 10-15 players, two hidden sides
what_the_game_is.crew: complete the task bar; impostors are a minority and hidden
what_the_game_is.impostor: kill crewmates until impostors equal or outnumber crewmates
phases: drop - everyone spawns, roles are assigned, no talking
task phase - free movement, no public chat, this is where kills happen
meeting - triggered by a body report or the emergency button; chat, then a vote
the vote ejects the highest-voted player; a tie or a Skip vote voids it
a meeting has a timer, normally 15-25s of discussion then a vote
what_the_game_is.two_vote_states: the same person can be voted twice in one meeting only if they survive the first vote; if they are ejected the meeting ends

ROLES.note: authoritative legality table. validate.py checks every turn against this.

Shapeshifter.special: mimic another player's appearance and name

Phantom.special: ability 1 = turn invisible; ability 2 = leave a decoy of yourself
Phantom.note: one of only TWO roles with a second ability

Viper.special: vents, and can kill from inside a vent at longer range

Scientist.special: Admin vitals: sees who is dead and who is disconnected

Engineer.special: vents for movement only, cannot kill

Guardian Angel.special: protects one player for the round
Guardian Angel.note: a ghost role. the bot only has this after dying

Tracker.special: track one player, shown on the map
Tracker.note: Tracker CANNOT vent. this is the single most common legality mistake

Noisemaker.special: place a decoy arrow that pulls players toward you

Detective.special: ability 1 = interrogate a player or inspect a body; ability 2 = read your notebook
Detective.note: one of only TWO roles with a second ability

Judge.special: one extra vote per game to eject a player
Judge.note: blocked from the overrule until your tasks are done

Phantom.special: ability 1 = vanish (usable by anyone, not only the killer); ability 2 = decoy
Phantom.note: Phantom can appear on EITHER side. as a crewmate it vents and cannot kill

hard_rules: no role has more than 2 abilities
only Impostor, Shapeshifter, Phantom, Viper, Engineer can vent
no impostor-side role should ever complete a real task
Guardian Angel only exists as a ghost, so it appears after a death

VENT_NETWORKS.note: vents connect in fixed groups. validate.py checks vent travel against this. Room names must be exact.

Polus.note: Polus vents are holes in the ground with no open/close animation, so a vent on Polus is much harder to spot being used

Airship.note: the Vault vent is a trap: cameras see you leave the Vault without entering it

Mira HQ.note: the only map where every vent reaches every other. the classic play is to vent, be seen, and cut the witness off before they reach Cafeteria

Fungle.note: a bean-shaped walk-around map with a moving layout, added 2024. rooms move between rounds, so treat room names as unstable

VENT_NETWORKS.universal: Communications has no vent on ANY map

why_this_matters: Wiring panels are numbered 1-7 and the correct colours always follow that
numbering. A fake that connects them in the wrong order is visibly wrong to
anyone who knows the pattern, and a model that learns the wrong order will
do it every time. Never write an entry that fakes wiring out of order.

fix_wiring.note: you get 3 of these 6 panels per game, in this fixed relative order. upper number to lower number on every panel
fix_wiring.wire_numbers: colours are ordered by a hidden number 1-7; connect lowest number to lowest
fix_wiring.correct_fake: stand at the panel for 3-4s per panel, in panel_order, connecting in number order

multi_stage_tasks.Fuel Engines: Storage -> Upper Engine -> back to Storage -> Lower Engine, 6s per stage
multi_stage_tasks.Align Engine Output: Upper Engine -> Lower Engine -> Reactor, 2-3s per stage
multi_stage_tasks.Fuel Engines (Polus): Storage -> Outside Electrical -> Administrative -> Boiler Room

timed_tasks_you_cannot_fake.note: the task bar only fills after the timer. leaving early is the tell
timed_tasks_you_cannot_fake.Inspect Sample: ~60s, timer keeps running if you walk away

visual_tasks.definition: other players can SEE the task happening, so standing still does not imitate it
visual_tasks.rule: never write an entry where the agent fakes a visual task by default. allow_visual only when the entry explains why the lesser evil was chosen
visual_tasks.note: Airship has NO visual tasks, which is why it is considered harder for crewmates

faking_rules: stand still for the REAL duration, sampled from the range, never a fixed constant
wait for the task bar to move before leaving, if a real task would have moved it
a fake never completes the task. the bar does not fill. the agent must report this honestly
common tasks are dangerous to fake: every player has them, so faking one you do not have proves you are the impostor

STRATEGY.note: the behaviour that actually wins. The non-verbal kill cycle matters more than talking, by a wide margin.

measured_evidence.source: MineAmongUs (2025), 1,344 matches, LLM/VLM agents playing Among Us
measured_evidence.headline: winners fake tasks 6.6x more often than losers. losers instead talk defensively, accuse their own teammate, and wander without purpose
measured_evidence.canonical_arc: fake a task -> stalk a target -> kill with no witness -> flee -> do NOT report the body -> next meeting: alibi + counter-accusation

impostor_kill_cycle: 1. FAKE first. The kill is the easy part; the meeting afterwards is what loses rounds. A fake buys cover and moves you across the map.
2. STALK. Follow someone at a distance. Know who has already seen you before you commit.
3. WITNESS CHECK. Never kill with someone in line of sight. If someone is near, back off and wait - do not kill and hope.
4. KILL, then FLEE immediately. Use the vent if there is one, otherwise round a corner. Standing near your own body is the worst possible position.
5. DO NOT REPORT. Strategic non-reporting is one of the strongest win correlates. Let someone else find it.

door_and_kill_tricks.close_doors_after_killing: in Storage or a room with a door, kill, then close the door. when the doors open later the room is empty and any witness inside has been absorbed into the group. works because crew re-open doors in a clump and nobody counts who was behind them
door_and_kill_tricks.why: a closed door hides both the body and the killer, and the delay lets other players move the group away from the scene

who_to_interrogate: anyone the game recorded as standing near a body you inspected - the notebook already lists them
the person who CHASED the victim. the 'who followed me' question catches more impostors than 'who was near the body'
anyone who was near the body and was ALREADY DEAD in the record - they were dead before the kill, so they were not the killer, but their last location matters
someone whose route does not connect their claimed task to where they were seen
who_not_to_interrogate: a random player with no connection to any body. this is the failure mode: interrogating strangers wastes the ability and teaches nothing
detective_play.how_to_use_it: interrogate -> read the notebook -> report ONLY what the notebook says. a detective that invents a theory is worse than one that stays quiet

phantom_play: ability 1 is vanish and is usable by ANY player, killer or not. using it as a crewmate is normal and buys you an alibi
ability 2 leaves a decoy arrow. as an impostor, decoy pulls crew toward a room you have already left
kill in a small room with a door, close the door, then vanish. the invisibility covers the window between the kill and the doors reopening
do not vanish while a witness is watching you do it - the animation is visible to anyone in vision
crew_play: the body is information. where it is, and who was near it, matters more than who 'felt' sus
walking with one other player is the single strongest survival action. two together is very hard to kill cleanly
if you did not see it, do not claim you did. a fabricated witness gets you ejected instead of the killer
skip the vote when you have no information. ejecting an innocent loses the round
the third-wheel play: if you see two people together, follow at a distance. if one kills, you are the witness. if nothing happens, both are probably fine

voting.early: with no evidence, skip is usually correct
voting.with_hard_evidence: someone who was seen on camera, or an admin/vitals confirmation, is a safe vote
voting.the_tie: a tie voids the meeting. if you are the impostor and someone is tying you, creating a tie is a win

DECEPTION.note: the measured linguistics of Among Us meetings. Vague deixis defensively, specific reference offensively.

vague_deixis.what: refer to people and places without naming them
vague_deixis.why: keeps you out of the crosshair; commits you to nothing checkable

specific_reference.what: when you attack, be concrete: player, room, and time
specific_reference.why: specificity reads as confidence, and confidence reads as truth
phrases: I saw blue in electrical just before the alarm
green was in medbay a minute ago

spatial_temporal_alibi.what: anchor yourself in a place and a time
spatial_temporal_alibi.why: concrete detail mimics the reality monitoring that marks real memories
phrases: I was in cafeteria when the body was found
I fixed lights before the reactor went off
spatial_temporal_alibi.warning: stay close to the truth. 'I was walking toward navigation' beats 'I was doing the upload in navigation', because if someone saw you in the hallway the bigger lie is instantly fatal

person_deixis.what: we/you/they manages who is in the group with you
person_deixis.why: inclusive 'we' builds trust, exclusive 'they' redirects blame
phrases: we all saw red vent, right?
if they keep ejecting randoms we're done

impostor_tactics.counter_accuse: answer an accusation with an accusation: 'you're trying to eject me off, it could be you'
impostor_tactics.self_report_pressure: 'it could be a self-report'. works because the reporter is always slightly sus, but use it once or people notice you always suggest it
impostor_tactics.throw_under_the_bus: accuse your own impostor partner to look credible and un-aligned. measurably common among winners
impostor_tactics.variation: change your defence each time. 'it wasn't me' repeated is a tell on its own
impostor_tactics.the_hard_lie: save 'I saw him vent' / 'I watched him kill' for when one eject ends the game. a vent claim is believed almost always - and if it is wrong, the person who made it is now the most suspicious person alive
impostor_tactics.emergency_button_as_weapon: an impostor calling a meeting is deeply unexpected, so it buys you a whole discussion to plant a name
impostor_tactics.fake_grief: complain about hard tasks, lag, or your card swipe glitching. you should sound bored, not nervous
impostor_tactics.go_quiet: say less than you want to. one cover lie is recoverable, a pile of them is not

crew_tactics.ask_who_saw: 'who did you see' is a better question than 'who is sus'
crew_tactics.ask_about_routes: 'what task were you doing' beats 'are you sus', because tasks are verifiable and vibes are not
crew_tactics.the_chase_question: 'who followed you' - this catches more impostors than any other single question
crew_tactics.separate_the_accused: stop the group from converging on one person before the evidence is in
crew_tactics.do_not_doubt_too_early: someone who let you live might be marinating you, building trust so you defend them at the end

real_player_moves: claiming a role: 'I'm engineer, I was venting' is nearly unattackable if true, and a very good lie if you are not
faking tears, anger, or eerie calm in the 3-player endgame
deliberately not reporting a body to watch who else finds it

SLANG.note: what players actually type. `say` arguments must read like these - short, lowercase, unpunctuated.

core.sus: suspicious. the central word of the game
core.mods: moderators, who can force a player to say a line
core.camping: waiting at a vent to kill whoever comes out
core.dead: dead, or a player who is dead
core.report: calling a meeting by reporting a body
core.self-report: reporting a body you killed yourself; also a jab at someone who always reports
core.hard lie: a claim of direct evidence, e.g. 'I saw him vent'
core.soft lie: a vague claim that cannot be checked
core.hard task: a long task, used as small talk to look innocent
core.fake: to pretend to do a task
core.dum: a player who is definitely not the impostor, said ironically
core.likely: a player who is probably the impostor
core.scan: Submit Scan, or the MedBay scanner
core.vitals: the Admin vitals, or the O2 room task list
core.admin: the Admin table, or the map on it
core.cams: security cameras, or the Security room
core.marinating: letting a suspected impostor live on purpose to seem trusting
core.chilling: standing still doing nothing on purpose
core.reactor hack: killing when the reactor is sabotaged and nobody can see the lights
core.spamming buttons: misclicking, a tell on some clients

phrases_that_sound_real: it could be a self report
style_rules: one claim per message, never a paragraph
no stage directions, no asterisks, no emoji
do not name-drop real-world players or use outside references
never write the impostor speaking in perfect prose - humans type fast and badly

TROPEES_AND_CLICHES.note: recognised patterns. Using them makes generated dialogue sound played rather than written.
impostor: the fake alibi that is one room too specific
accusing the person who accused you, immediately
the 'I have admin' claim with nothing behind it
the hard lie saved for the perfect moment, then spending it too early
killing in a two-vent room so there is always an escape
self-reporting because the reporter is always slightly sus
the partner who accuses the other impostor to look credible
going quiet after talking too much
killing during a lights sabotage so nobody can see
crew: the silent player everyone converges on by the third meeting
the overconfident eject that removes an innocent
the group trying to un-eject someone for the rest of the round
'who was near the body' said by three people at once
trusting the player who vouched for them last round
the final 1v1 where both players are silent
someone who was right once and is never believed again
structural: the first meeting is chaos, the second is the real one
the impostor's best round is the one nobody accuses anyone in
a tie vote is a guaranteed impostor win
the game is effectively decided by the third meeting

AGENT_FAILURE_MODES.note: what the base model gets wrong, and what an entry must counteract. If you are writing an entry, you are fixing one of these.

known_failures.what_happens: the impostor says 'I am the impostor and I am standing right here'
known_failures.counter: never write an entry where the impostor volunteers its own identity

known_failures.what_happens: the agent claims a witness who does not exist, wasting the turn
known_failures.counter: only name players present in the situation line

known_failures.what_happens: two impostors vote for each other
known_failures.counter: in any entry with two impostors, write them voting to clear themselves

known_failures.what_happens: chases only crewmates who are never alone, so every kill ends in a retreat
an impostor that spends the whole round in meetings and never fakes a task loses, per the measured data
known_failures.counter: every impostor entry must contain at least one fake_task

known_failures.failure: fake wiring in the wrong colour order
known_failures.what_happens: visibly wrong to anyone who knows the pattern
wastes the ability on a random player

known_failures.failure: phantom killing in a room with an open door
known_failures.what_happens: a witness walks in during the kill animation
